perf-resources.title: Performance & Resource Efficiency
perf-resources.description: Fix CPU hotspots (O(n^2) algorithms, redundant traversals), memory waste (unnecessary allocations in release builds), IO inefficiency (per-event flush), resource management bugs (flush semantics, exception safety), and build config (R8 shrinking). Based on double-design review (Claude + Codex), revalidated 2026-04-16.
acceptCriteria: All child tasks done
./gradlew assembleDebug passes
./gradlew test passes

perf-r8-minify.title: Enable R8 minification and resource shrinking
perf-r8-minify.description: Release build has isMinifyEnabled=false, shipping dead code from OpenAI SDK, OkHttp, Compose, Leap SDK etc. Enable R8 tree shaking + resource shrinking. Key challenge: writing correct keep rules for kotlinx.serialization (session persistence JSON), Shizuku AIDL interfaces, OpenAI SDK reflection patterns, and Leap SDK JNI methods. Start with proguard-android-optimize.txt defaults, add targeted keep rules, then iteratively fix any runtime ClassNotFoundException/NoSuchMethodError via release APK smoke test.
acceptCriteria: app/build.gradle.kts release block has isMinifyEnabled=true and isShrinkResources=true
app/proguard-rules.pro exists with keep rules for serialization, Shizuku, OpenAI SDK, Leap SDK

./gradlew test passes

perf-history-compression.title: Fix history compression O(n^2) token recalculation
perf-history-compression.description: HistoryManager.compress() eviction loop calls estimateTokenCount() on every iteration, but every removeAt() sets lastTokenEstimate=null, forcing a full items.sumOf{it.estimateTokens()} rescan. This is O(n^2) in history size. Fix: maintain a running token total during Phase 2 eviction. Before the while loop, capture runningTokens=estimateTokenCount(). On each removal, subtract the removed item tokens. After eviction completes, set lastTokenEstimate=null to invalidate cache for external callers. Same pattern needed for Phase 3 (group eviction) if it also loops on estimateTokenCount().
acceptCriteria: compress() Phase 2 loop uses delta tracking instead of full rescan per removal
No call to estimateTokenCount() inside the eviction while-loop body
lastTokenEstimate invalidated only once after eviction completes, not per removal
Unit test: compress large history (500+ items over budget) — token count after compress matches items.sumOf{it.estimateTokens()}
Unit test: compress with mixed item types (screen observations, tool outputs, user messages) — correct items evicted per existing priority rules
Existing HistoryManager tests still pass
./gradlew test passes

perf-truncation-indexof.title: Fix truncation O(n^2) indexOf in applyTruncation
perf-truncation-indexof.description: applyTruncation() in PerceptorInternals.kt calls candidates.indexOf(c) in three loops (interactive, non-interactive, fallback). Each indexOf is O(n) with expensive data-class equals(). With maxElements=500 and 2x over-collection (up to 1000 candidates), this is up to 500K comparisons. Fix: use a HashSet<PerceptorCandidateElement> for dedup instead of position-based indexOf. Build a "seen" set, add elements as they are selected. The kept list preserves insertion order (priority ordering). This also simplifies the code — no need to track indices at all.
acceptCriteria: applyTruncation() contains zero calls to candidates.indexOf()
Dedup uses HashSet or equivalent O(1) lookup instead of linear scan
Unit test: truncation with 1000 synthetic candidates — same output elements as before (order-preserving)
Unit test: interactive elements get priority up to interactiveKeepRatio cap
Unit test: no duplicate elements in output
Unit test: candidates.size <= maxElements returns input unchanged (early exit)
./gradlew test passes

perf-trace-flush.title: Fix FileTraceRecorder flush() semantics + add write batching
perf-trace-flush.description: Two co-dependent issues: (IO-1) AppendLine handler calls writer.flush() on every event, defeating BufferedWriter batching. (RES-2) WriteOp.Flush handler only completes the deferred without calling writer.flush() — the public flush() API promises durability but delivers only a queue barrier. These MUST be co-fixed: removing per-line flush makes the broken Flush handler user-visible. Fix: (a) In WriteOp.Flush handler, call writer.flush() before completing the deferred. (b) Remove writer.flush() from AppendLine handler. (c) Optionally flush on batch threshold (every 10 lines or when channel.isEmpty) for reasonable latency.
acceptCriteria: WriteOp.AppendLine handler does NOT call writer.flush()
WriteOp.Flush handler calls writer.flush() BEFORE completing op.done
Writer is flushed in the finally block (on channel close/writer close)
Unit test: write 100 events then flush() — all 100 lines present in file after flush returns
Unit test: write events without explicit flush — file may be partially buffered (batching works)
Unit test: close() flushes remaining buffered content to disk
./gradlew test passes

perf-streaming-guard.title: Guard streaming accumulation behind verbose logging flag
perf-streaming-guard.description: All three streaming LLM clients (CodexResponseClient, OpenAIResponseClient, ChatCompletionClient) unconditionally build StringBuilder accumulators and tool-call lists for LlmLogger.logOutput(), which returns immediately in release builds. Fix: expose LlmLogger.isVerboseEnabled (= VERBOSE_LOGGING). In each streaming client, only allocate the text StringBuilder and completed tool-call buffers when isVerboseEnabled is true. Keep delta emission and tool call tracking for the actual response flow unchanged — only the logging-specific accumulators are guarded.
acceptCriteria: LlmLogger exposes a public isVerboseEnabled property (or equivalent)
StringBuilder/tool-call accumulators only allocated when verbose logging is enabled
Streaming delta emission to downstream collectors is unchanged regardless of verbose flag
logOutput() still called with full data when verbose logging IS enabled (debug builds)
No ResponsesResult object constructed in non-verbose mode
./gradlew test passes
./gradlew assembleDebug passes

perf-baos-presize.title: Pre-size ByteArrayOutputStream for JPEG compression
perf-baos-presize.description: BitmapUtils.compressJpeg() uses ByteArrayOutputStream() with default 32-byte buffer, causing 10-12 reallocation+copy cycles for typical 50-150KB JPEGs. Fix: pre-size with an estimate based on pixel count. Use (bitmap.width * bitmap.height * 4) / 10 as initial capacity (ARGB pixels / ~10 for JPEG compression ratio), clamped to 1KB-512KB range to avoid over-allocation for tiny or huge bitmaps.
acceptCriteria: ByteArrayOutputStream in compressJpeg() is constructed with a capacity estimate, not default
Capacity estimate is clamped to a reasonable range (minimum 1KB, maximum 512KB)
JPEG output bytes are identical to before (compression behavior unchanged)
./gradlew assembleDebug passes

perf-single-pass-perceptor.title: Single-pass Perceptor tree traversal
perf-single-pass-perceptor.description: Perceptor.snapshot() traverses every accessibility root twice: once in INTERACTIVE_ONLY mode, then again in ALL mode. Each traverse() reads text/description/hint/resource ID, action support, bounds, visibility ratio, and class name per node. For 300-500 nodes with 2-3 roots, this doubles the work on the hottest capture path. Fix: merge into a single traversal that collects all eligible nodes in one pass, tagging each as interactive or non-interactive. The existing applyTruncation() already handles interactive/non-interactive separation via interactiveKeepRatio, so prioritization is preserved. Key constraint: the seenKeys dedup must still work correctly — currently it prevents duplicates across both passes, so the single pass must use the same dedup logic. Validate by comparing snapshot output (element counts, interactive coverage, element ordering) before and after.
acceptCriteria: snapshot() contains exactly one traversal loop over roots (not two)
TraversalMode enum still exists but single pass uses unified criteria
Interactive elements are still prioritized in truncation (interactiveKeepRatio preserved)
Unit test: snapshot parity — same elements returned as before for representative tree fixtures
Unit test: interactive coverage — same number of interactive elements kept after truncation
Unit test: seenKeys dedup — no duplicate elements in output
Unit test: empty tree and single-root tree edge cases
./gradlew test passes

perf-text-enrichment.title: Optimize text enrichment from O(n^2) to sub-quadratic
perf-text-enrichment.description: enrichEmptyTextElements() scans all textSources for every interactive element needing text. With maxElements=500 and 2x over-collection, this can be up to 1000*1000 containment checks plus mergedText() recomputation. Two viable approaches: (A) Build a simple spatial index once (e.g., sort textSources by top-left coordinate, binary search for candidates within bounds), or (B) Propagate text from parent/sibling during the single traversal pass (if perf-single-pass-perceptor is done first). Approach B is cleaner but couples to the traversal refactor. Approach A is standalone. Either way, cache mergedText() per source to avoid recomputation in the inner loop. Product-sensitive: text enrichment affects what the LLM sees for unlabeled buttons, so output parity testing is critical.
acceptCriteria: enrichEmptyTextElements() no longer does O(n*m) full scan of textSources per interactive element
mergedText() result is cached per source (not recomputed in inner loop)
Unit test: enrichment parity — same text assigned to same elements as before for representative fixtures
Unit test: nested button inside labeled container — button gets container text
Unit test: button with no nearby text source — remains unenriched (no false positives)
Unit test: performance — 1000 candidates completes in <100ms (was potentially seconds)
./gradlew test passes

perf-bitmap-safety.title: Make bitmap cleanup exception-safe in screenshot pipeline
perf-bitmap-safety.description: AccessibilityScreenshotCapturer.compressScreenshot() only guarantees hardwareBuffer.close() in finally. hardwareBitmap, softwareBitmap, and scaledBitmap are recycled on the normal path only. If an exception occurs between allocation and recycle (e.g., during bitmap copy or JPEG compression), the native bitmap allocations (~10MB each) remain until GC. The leak window is narrow (hardwareBitmap is recycled immediately after copy, others before debug persistence) but worth hardening. Fix: wrap each bitmap in nested try/finally or use a local cleanup helper that tracks allocated bitmaps and recycles all on any exit path.
acceptCriteria: All intermediate bitmaps (hardwareBitmap, softwareBitmap, scaledBitmap) are recycled on both normal and exceptional paths
hardwareBuffer.close() still in finally block
No double-recycle — identity check (scaledBitmap !== softwareBitmap) preserved
Normal-path behavior unchanged — screenshot capture still produces correct ScreenImage
./gradlew assembleDebug passes
./gradlew test passes

perf-streaming-cancel.title: Add cancellation hooks to remaining streaming LLM clients
perf-streaming-cancel.description: CodexResponseClient already stores activeCall and cancels it from awaitClose (fixed previously). OpenAIResponseClient and ChatCompletionClient still only log from awaitClose — no active stream/call handle is stored, so flow cancellation cannot proactively stop in-flight network reads or retry cycles. Fix: follow the CodexResponseClient pattern — store a reference to the active call/stream, cancel it from awaitClose. For OpenAIResponseClient (uses OpenAI Java SDK), check if the SDK exposes a cancellable stream handle. For ChatCompletionClient (uses OkHttp directly), store the Call reference like CodexResponseClient does. Ensure retry loops check for cancellation.
acceptCriteria: OpenAIResponseClient stores active stream/call handle and cancels from awaitClose
ChatCompletionClient stores active Call reference and cancels from awaitClose (matching CodexResponseClient pattern)
Retry loops in both clients check for cancellation before retrying
Normal streaming still works — tool calls and text deltas emitted correctly
./gradlew assembleDebug passes
./gradlew test passes

error-resilience.title: Error Resilience 改进
error-resilience.description: Fix cross-layer error semantics: false completion reporting, approval failure swallowing, delegate_task masking, shutdown ANR, action state flattening, and missing TASK_IMPOSSIBLE. Based on verified double-design review (Claude + Codex), revalidated 2026-04-15.
acceptCriteria: All child tasks done
./gradlew test passes
./gradlew assembleDebug passes

er-completion-correctness.title: P0: Make completion depend on executed tool results
er-completion-correctness.description:
AgentTurnRunner.decideCompletion() uses planned tool calls, not executed results. TurnExecutionPhaseRunner.executeActions() returns Unit — the runner has no way to know if complete_task actually ran.

Concrete bug: Model plans remember_experience → complete_task(success). remember_experience fails, execution loop breaks, complete_task never runs. But decideCompletion() only checks planned tools, so the turn reports Complete(success=true).

Fix: Return minimal execution metadata from executeActions() — which tool IDs actually executed, whether execution terminated early, and the terminal result. AgentTurnRunner checks that complete_task is in the executed set before emitting TurnOutcome.Complete. If execution broke before complete_task, emit TurnOutcome.Error or TurnOutcome.Cancelled based on the actual terminal result.

Keep it minimal: only add enough data to answer 'did complete_task actually run and succeed?'
acceptCriteria: executeActions() returns a result type containing the set of tool IDs that actually executed
decideCompletion() checks that complete_task is in the executed set before emitting TurnOutcome.Complete
When complete_task is planned but execution breaks before it runs, the turn emits TurnOutcome.Error (not Complete)
When complete_task runs and succeeds, behavior unchanged from current
Test: mock remember_experience failure before complete_task → TurnOutcome is Error, not Complete
Test: complete_task executes normally → TurnOutcome.Complete as before
Test: no complete_task in plan, all tools succeed → TurnOutcome.Continue as before
grep -q 'executedToolIds\|ExecutionPhaseResult\|executionResult' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/agent/TurnExecutionPhaseRunner.kt
./gradlew test passes

er-approval-failfast.title: P0: Fail fast when approval UI dispatch breaks
er-approval-failfast.description:
TurnExecutionPhaseRunner.emitApprovalRequired() (lines 164-174) wraps the event emitter call in try/catch and swallows exceptions with Log.e(). ToolRouter is already prepared to convert approval-dispatch exceptions into ToolCallResult.Error, but never sees them because emitApprovalRequired suppresses the throw.

Result: if the approval UI/overlay fails to display, the tool waits 60 seconds then returns 'Approval timed out' — blaming the user for not responding to a prompt they never saw.

Fix: Remove the try/catch in emitApprovalRequired(). Let the exception propagate to ToolRouter, which already handles it by returning ToolCallResult.Error('Approval request failed: ...'). This is a ~5-line change — delete the try/catch wrapper, keep the event emission.
acceptCriteria: emitApprovalRequired() no longer has a try/catch that swallows exceptions
When event emitter throws, ToolRouter returns ToolCallResult.Error (not Cancelled/timeout)
The error message includes 'Approval request failed' or similar diagnostic text
Normal approval flow (no exception) is unchanged
Test: mock eventEmitter that throws → tool result is Error, not Cancelled
Test: normal eventEmitter → approval wait proceeds as before
! grep -q 'catch.*emitApproval\|catch.*approval.*Exception' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/agent/TurnExecutionPhaseRunner.kt || echo 'swallow removed'
./gradlew test passes

er-delegate-failure.title: P0: Return structural failure from delegate_task
er-delegate-failure.description:
DelegateTaskTool (lines 164-177) returns textToolSuccess(...) even when result.success is false. This means: (1) action cards show the delegation as successful, (2) history records it as successful, (3) parent turn control flow cannot distinguish healthy delegation from failed delegation except by parsing text. With PRO mode as default agent mode, this is a core orchestration bug.

Fix: When result.success is false, return a failure result type (e.g., ToolExecutionResult.Failure or textToolError) instead of textToolSuccess. Reserve textToolSuccess exclusively for successful delegations. Keep the sub-agent output message in the result so the parent LLM can still read what happened.
acceptCriteria: When sub-agent result.success is false, DelegateTaskTool returns a failure/error result (not textToolSuccess)
When sub-agent result.success is true, DelegateTaskTool returns textToolSuccess as before
The failure result still contains the sub-agent's output message for parent LLM context
Test: mock sub-agent failure → tool result is Error/Failure type, not Success
Test: mock sub-agent success → tool result is Success
! grep -A5 'result.success.*false\|!result.success' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/tool/impl/DelegateTaskTool.kt | grep -q 'textToolSuccess' || echo 'success-on-failure removed'
./gradlew test passes

er-ondestroy-anr.title: P0: Move onDestroy() shutdown off main thread
er-ondestroy-anr.description:
AgentService.onDestroy() (lines 206-237) uses runBlocking { withTimeoutOrNull(5000) { ... submit(Op.Shutdown) ... } }. This blocks the main thread for up to 5 seconds during service restart, risking ANR.

The naive fix of scope.launch { shutdown } + scope.cancel() won't work — cancelling the scope kills the launched shutdown coroutine.

Fix: Use a dedicated shutdown scope that outlives the service scope. Options:
- CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Default) with its own 5s timeout, then cancel
- GlobalScope.launch(NonCancellable + Dispatchers.Default) with timeout

The session already handles checkpoint persistence via NonCancellable in deliverCompletion, so partial shutdown is tolerable — the main goal is avoiding the main-thread block.
acceptCriteria: onDestroy() does not call runBlocking on the main thread
Shutdown Op is dispatched to a scope/coroutine that is not immediately cancelled by onDestroy()
Shutdown still has a bounded timeout (≤5s) to prevent leaked coroutines
Normal service teardown still cleans up overlayController, scope, etc.
! grep -q 'runBlocking' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/app/AgentService.kt
./gradlew test passes
./gradlew assembleDebug passes

er-task-impossible.title: P1: Split TASK_IMPOSSIBLE from internal ERROR
er-task-impossible.description:
CompletionReason.TASK_IMPOSSIBLE exists in protocol and UI/recording layers are wired for it. But AgentStopReason has no TaskImpossible variant. When complete_task(status='failure') is called, Agent.kt maps it to AgentStopReason.Error, and AgentSession maps that to CompletionReason.ERROR. The distinction between 'system fault' and 'agent concluded task is impossible' is thrown away.

Fix: Add AgentStopReason.TaskImpossible(message: String). In Agent.kt, convert TurnOutcome.Complete(success=false) to TaskImpossible instead of Error. In AgentSession.toCompletionReason(), map TaskImpossible to CompletionReason.TASK_IMPOSSIBLE.

This depends on er-completion-correctness because that task changes how completion outcomes flow through AgentTurnRunner — the mapping point for success/failure must be stable first.
acceptCriteria: AgentStopReason.TaskImpossible(message: String) exists in AgentRuntimeTypes.kt
Agent.kt maps TurnOutcome.Complete(success=false) to AgentStopReason.TaskImpossible
AgentSession.toCompletionReason() maps TaskImpossible to CompletionReason.TASK_IMPOSSIBLE
Agent.kt maps TurnOutcome.Complete(success=true) to GoalAchieved (unchanged)
Test: complete_task(status=failure) → CompletionReason is TASK_IMPOSSIBLE, not ERROR
Test: complete_task(status=success) → CompletionReason is GOAL_ACHIEVED (unchanged)
Test: real agent error (LLM throws) → CompletionReason is still ERROR
grep -q 'TaskImpossible' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/agent/AgentRuntimeTypes.kt
./gradlew test passes

er-harden-cleanup.title: P1: Harden cleanup and observation fallback
er-harden-cleanup.description:
Two independent hardening fixes:

(A) SessionServices.cleanup() (lines 210-237): only platform.stop() is guarded with try/catch. llmClient.cleanup(), llmClientFactory.cleanupAll(), and traceRecorder.close() are unguarded — if any throws, teardown aborts mid-sequence and later cleanup steps never run.

Fix A: Wrap each cleanup call independently with try/catch + Log.w. Continue cleanup regardless of individual failures.

(B) TurnExecutionPhaseRunner.captureObservationWithSnapshot() (lines 210-235): called after tool failures without shielding. If screen capture throws (e.g., accessibility service disconnected), a local tool failure escalates to a turn-level failure. Error handling should not itself be fragile.

Fix B: Wrap captureObservationWithSnapshot() in runCatching. On failure, fall back to ToolObservation.TextOutput(result.toContextString()) with no new snapshot — the agent still gets the tool result text and can continue.
acceptCriteria: Every cleanup call in SessionServices.cleanup() is individually guarded with try/catch
If llmClient.cleanup() throws, llmClientFactory.cleanupAll() and traceRecorder.close() still execute
captureObservationWithSnapshot() is wrapped in runCatching (or equivalent try/catch)
When screen capture fails after a tool failure, the turn continues with a text-only observation
Test: mock llmClient.cleanup() throw → remaining cleanup steps still run
Test: mock captureScreen() throw during observation → turn gets text-only observation, no crash
./gradlew test passes

er-action-outcome.title: P1: Preserve action outcome semantics end to end
er-action-outcome.description:
ActionExecuted carries only success: Boolean, collapsing policy denial, user denial, approval timeout, and real execution failure into the same 'failed' bucket. TurnExecutionPhaseRunner emits '✓ <tool> executed' status even for failed actions. ActionState.Skipped exists in UI model but is never used.

Fix: Replace Boolean success with a three-value enum:
  enum class ActionOutcome { SUCCESS, FAILED, SKIPPED }

Derive from ToolCallResult type (no string matching):
- ToolCallResult.Success → SUCCESS
- ToolCallResult.Error → FAILED
- ToolCallResult.Cancelled → SKIPPED

Update ActionExecuted, TurnExecutionPhaseRunner (status emission), AgentServiceEventHandler, and ChatEventReducer to use the enum. Only show ✓ checkmark for SUCCESS. Wire ActionState.Skipped for SKIPPED results.
acceptCriteria: ActionExecuted uses an enum (ActionOutcome or similar) instead of Boolean success
ToolCallResult.Success maps to SUCCESS, Error to FAILED, Cancelled to SKIPPED
TurnExecutionPhaseRunner only emits ✓ status for SUCCESS outcomes
ChatEventReducer maps SKIPPED to ActionState.Skipped (which already exists in the model)
AgentServiceEventHandler distinguishes failed from skipped in history recording
Test: ToolCallResult.Cancelled → ActionExecuted has SKIPPED outcome
Test: ToolCallResult.Error → ActionExecuted has FAILED outcome
Test: ToolCallResult.Success → ActionExecuted has SUCCESS outcome, ✓ status emitted
grep -q 'ActionOutcome\|SKIPPED' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/protocol/ActionEvents.kt
./gradlew test passes

er-bootstrap-ux.title: P1: Improve bootstrap/session failure UX
er-bootstrap-ux.description:
When session creation or LLM bootstrap fails, the error surfaces only as toast/overlay status text. The user's input text only enters chat on TaskStarted — if startup fails before that event, the input disappears from chat history. The user has no clear path to retry.

Fix (scope tightly to three changes):
1. Preserve the user's pending input text when session creation fails — store it so it can be re-submitted or at least displayed
2. Surface startup failure as a visible error state in the main chat/session UI (not just toast)
3. Provide explicit retry/reload affordance

Key files: ChatViewModel handles the submission flow, AgentSession.initializeForFirstTask() is the failure point, ChatEventReducer needs to handle a new 'startup failed' state.
acceptCriteria: When session creation fails, user's input text is preserved (not silently dropped)
Startup failure is visible in chat UI as an error message (not just toast/overlay)
User can retry the failed input without retyping it
Normal session startup flow is unchanged
Test: mock bootstrap failure → chat shows error state with user's original input preserved
./gradlew test passes
./gradlew assembleDebug passes

er-dead-error-surface.title: P2: Clean up dead typed error surface
er-dead-error-surface.description:
AgentError.kt defines 11 error variants (LLMError, PlatformError, PermissionError, etc.) and SessionLifecycleEvents.kt defines SessionError. Neither is produced by the live runtime — all error paths use TurnErrorClassifier → strings → CompletionReason.ERROR.

After P0/P1 fixes land (completion correctness, TASK_IMPOSSIBLE, action outcome), reassess what typed error structure the runtime actually needs. Two options:
(a) Delete dead types — the semantic fixes already address the concrete problems
(b) Replace with 3-4 live variants used only where structure materially helps (e.g., LLMError, PlatformError, PolicyError)

Decide based on what gaps remain after P0/P1.
acceptCriteria: AgentError.kt either deleted or trimmed to ≤4 variants that are actually produced by runtime code
If AgentError is kept, at least one call site instantiates each remaining variant
SessionError either deleted or wired to at least one emitter
No dead sealed class variants (every variant has a producer)
grep -c 'AgentError\.' app/src/main/kotlin/com/moonkey/androidagent/**/*.kt shows usage for every remaining variant (or file is deleted)
./gradlew test passes

er-corrupted-history.title: P2: Surface corrupted session history entries
er-corrupted-history.description:
Session writes are now atomic (temp+rename). The remaining issue is read-side: SessionHistoryManager.extractSessionInfo() returns null when it can't parse a session file, and the manager silently drops the entry from the list. Users get no explanation for missing sessions.

Fix: When extractSessionInfo() fails to parse, return a placeholder SessionInfo (or error wrapper) that surfaces in the session list instead of being silently omitted. Add read-time diagnostics logging so corrupted files can be investigated.
acceptCriteria: When a session file can't be parsed, a placeholder entry appears in the session list (not silently dropped)
The placeholder shows the file name and an indication that the session is corrupted/unreadable
Corrupted session parse failures are logged at warning level with the file name and exception
Normal session files still load and display correctly
Test: write a malformed session file → session list shows placeholder entry for it
./gradlew test passes

er-context-length-msg.title: P2: User-friendly context-length error message
er-context-length-msg.description:
TurnErrorClassifier (lines 32-50) correctly detects context-length errors via keyword matching and marks them non-recoverable. But the message surfaced to the user is the raw provider text (e.g., 'This model's maximum context length is 128000 tokens'). No actionable guidance.

Fix: When isContextLimit is true, override the message with a user-friendly string like 'Conversation too long for model context window. Try starting a new task or reducing the number of turns.' Keep the raw message in the log for debugging.
acceptCriteria: When isContextLimit is true, the returned TurnErrorClassification.message is a user-friendly string (not raw API text)
The user-friendly message includes actionable guidance (e.g., 'start a new task')
The raw provider error is still logged at warning/error level for debugging
Non-context-limit errors are unchanged
Test: exception with 'maximum context length' → user-facing message is friendly, not raw API text
./gradlew test passes

perf-qa-real-device.title: QA Round: Real Device Validation
perf-qa-real-device.description: Run end-to-end QA on real device to validate perf-resources changes do not regress agent behavior. Test scenarios: (1) Normal multi-turn task — agent completes a 5+ turn task without errors, verify perception captures correct elements (single-pass Perceptor validation). (2) Dense screen capture — open an app with 300+ UI elements, verify truncation returns correct interactive elements and text enrichment labels unlabeled buttons. (3) Long session — run 15+ turns to trigger history compression, verify session completes and history is coherent (no missing turns). (4) Release APK smoke test — install release build, run a simple task end-to-end (validates R8 keep rules in production). (5) Trace recording — enable tracing, run a task, verify trace file is complete and flush semantics work (last events present after session end). Use /ux-visual-debug or adb-driven interaction.
acceptCriteria: QA report exists with pass/fail per scenario at doc/todo/holistic-review/performance-resources/qa_report.md
Normal multi-turn task: completes without error, correct elements captured
Dense screen: truncation returns expected interactive element count, enriched text matches visible labels
Long session: 15+ turns with compression — no missing turns, session history coherent
Release APK: installs, starts, completes a task without crash or ClassNotFoundException
Trace recording: trace file contains all expected events, no truncation at end
No ANR or crash in logcat during QA run

er-qa-real-device.title: QA Round: Real Device Validation
er-qa-real-device.description:
Run end-to-end QA on real device to validate error-resilience fixes don't regress user-facing behavior and the correctness bugs are actually fixed. Test scenarios:

(1) False completion: trigger a task where a cognitive tool fails before complete_task — verify the agent does NOT report success
(2) Approval dispatch: simulate overlay failure during approval-gated action — verify error is immediate (not 60s timeout)
(3) Delegate failure: trigger a PRO-mode task where sub-agent fails — verify parent sees failure, not success in action card
(4) Service restart: force-stop the service mid-task, relaunch — verify no ANR, session recovers
(5) Action outcome display: trigger a policy-denied action — verify UI shows skipped (not ✓ executed)
(6) Task impossible: give the agent an impossible task — verify CompletionReason is TASK_IMPOSSIBLE in session history
(7) Normal multi-turn task: complete a standard task — verify no regression

Use /ux-visual-debug or adb-driven interaction.
acceptCriteria: QA report exists with pass/fail per scenario (doc/todo/holistic-review/error-resilience/qa_report.md)
False completion: agent reports error/failure when complete_task didn't execute
Approval dispatch failure: error returned immediately, no 60s hang
Delegate failure: parent action card shows failure, not success
Service restart: no ANR in logcat, session checkpoint loads correctly
Action outcome: skipped/denied actions show correct state in chat UI (not ✓)
Task impossible: session history shows TASK_IMPOSSIBLE reason
Normal multi-turn task: completes without regression
No ANR or crash in logcat during QA run
